findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark and will never be invoked
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers in this codebase gate conditional attributes with methods named `include_<attribute>?`, as seen in include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, and the methods generated by untrusted_attributes. The new method is named `include_website_name` without `?`, so the serializer will not call it and `website_name` will be emitted (as nil when there is no parseable host) even when `website` is blank, defeating the intended conditional inclusion.

findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction for TL0 users viewed anonymously
findings.body: `website` is listed in untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111), which suppresses it for trust-level-0 users seen by anonymous visitors. The newly added `website_name` is derived directly from `website` but is not added to that list, and its (misnamed) include method adds no restriction, so anonymous visitors can still learn a TL0 user's website host and, in the same-domain case, its full path even though the underlying website field is deliberately hidden from them.

findings.title: Same-domain detection is asymmetric for www hostnames
findings.body: When the website is `www.example.com/path` and the instance host is `example.com`, the first branch fails (hosts differ), the second branch fails (segment counts 3 vs 2 differ), and the else branch checks whether `example.com` ends with `.www.example.com`, which is false, so only the host is shown. The reverse combination (website `example.com/path`, instance `www.example.com`) does show the full path via the suffix check. The 'same domain' UX therefore depends on which side carries the www prefix, contradicting the PR goal; the sibling-subdomain branch (www vs forum) is also untested.

findings.title: Tests cover neither the anonymous TL0 leak nor the subdomain branches of website_name
findings.body: The new specs only cover exact-host match, parent-host match, and unrelated hosts for a regular user. The untrusted_attributes list in the TL0/anonymous context is unchanged and no example asserts website_name is hidden there, and there is no example for the equal-length subdomain branch in the serializer (e.g. website www.example.com vs instance forum.example.com, or the asymmetric www-vs-bare-domain cases), so the privacy regression and the hostname-matching edge cases would pass CI undetected.
